svg.text: THE FASTENER SANDWICH AT ONE MAGNET
True section through one magnet position, drawn at one scale on both axes - 4.6 px/mm across AND through. One drawing per fastener combination.
Plate 4.75 mm (0.187 in), hole O8.5 mm, stud a fixed 12.70 mm (0.500 in). Change any of those and every panel here changes with it.
The orange band is where that part actually touches the plate. Part numbers are McMaster-Carr, read off their tables on 2026-08-27.
Washer thickness is a RANGE (0.89-1.75 mm), not a nominal - every stack here is checked against the THICKEST one you might be shipped.

USE: THIN nylon-insert locknut, no washer
The washer is worth having: it spreads the clamp over 225 mm2 instead of a bare nut's 70 mm2 - 3.2x the area, 389 psi less on the plate. The question was only ever whether it FITS.

You can have LOCKING or the washer, not both: the thin nyloc misses with a washer by 0.15 mm. Locking wins - the bare nut's 565 psi is still 64x under yield, so the washer is comfort, while a nut backing off under touch-cycling is a real failure.
Runner-up: the distorted-thread locknut is the SAME 6.75 mm height as a plain hex nut - locking for nothing - but it is not reusable and is not stocked in black.
Fasteners are specified in BLACK OXIDE throughout: only the ARM nuts are visible, and they face up against a matte-black arm.
